Biggest problems from ethanol: metal corrosion, it contains much less energy than gas, and it likes water.

On a car made in the last 25 years, you should be fine with 10% ethanol. On older stuff carburetor parts block up and all sorts of metals can corrode.

To run E85, your fueling system needs to put in more fuel, so you need to upgrade injectors and/or computers. Also, since E85 isn't always 85% ethanol, and when it absorbs water, the 15% gas can separate out, you need a sensor to tell you just how much ethanol you are burning. E85 has even more ethanol than the 10% stuff, so you can't get by with just coating metal, you need stainless. Some rubber is more likely to swell as well.
